svg.title: Rival Alliance Blocs & The Balkan Powder Keg (1879 – August 1914)
svg.desc: KS3 historical GIS atlas map of 1914 Europe showing the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy), the encircling Triple Entente (France, Russia, and Great Britain), Austria-Hungary’s October 1908 annexation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, expanded Serbia and the 28 June 1914 Sarajevo assassination, and the August 1914 German Schlieffen invasion through Neutral Belgium.

text.tspan: France, Russia & Britain create two-front nightmare
Balkan Wars double Serbia; Archduke shot
Aug 1914 invasion breaks 1839 Treaty & brings Britain in

g.text: KEY • ALLIANCE BLOCS & BALKAN POWDER KEG
Kingdom of Italy (1882 Ally • Stays Neutral 1914)

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: CAUSES OF THE GREAT WAR
Rival Alliance Blocs & The Balkan Powder Keg (1879 – Aug 1914)
Rival alliances split Europe into two armed camps, turning the 1908 Bosnian Crisis and 1912–13 Balkan Wars into a powder keg.
After Sarajevo (28 June 1914), interlocking treaties & Germany’s Schlieffen march through Belgium pulled Britain into world war.
